taxonomy.name: Contractual Income
taxonomy.description: Cashflow is primarily defined by contract. Main risks are duration, credit quality, reinvestment and FX rather than operating execution.

subcategories.name: Investment Grade Credit
examples: AAA / AA / A / BBB corporate bonds

taxonomy.name: Productive Distribution
taxonomy.description: Cashflow comes from productive businesses or listed real assets. Income depends on earnings, asset quality, leverage and payout policy.

taxonomy.name: Illiquid Real Assets
taxonomy.description: Cashflow is tied to physical assets and local operating conditions. Valuation is slower, transaction costs are high and liquidity can disappear.

taxonomy.name: Engineered Yield
taxonomy.description: Cashflow is manufactured by selling optionality, locking capital or taking protocol / counterparty risk. Yield can be high because risk is explicitly sold.

methodology.valuation: Invest 100 at the beginning of the window, hold, do not reinvest distributions, and mark to current value.
methodology.option_income: Current seller-executable bid is mechanically annualized by 365/DTE. BTC and ETH use Deribit; listed US options prefer CBOE delayed Greeks/quotes with a Yahoo fallback. Daily snapshots build the historical estimate series.
methodology.staking_income: ETH staking uses the current Lido stETH 7-day simple-moving-average APR; it is a protocol yield estimate, not a guaranteed return.
methodology.best_strategy: Option matrices rank premium yield divided by |delta|^1.2, adjusted for DTE, IV versus recent realized volatility, and liquidity.
methodology.risk_ladder: Layers 1→4 are a conceptual progression in cashflow complexity, operating dependence, illiquidity and actively sold risk. They are not universal loss-probability ratings.
